key_insight: Combining physics-based simulation and neural networks identified a favorable HDPE friction stir welding condition of 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports process-window selection to reduce weld defects, thermal gradients and axial force fluctuations in HDPE joints.
method: Develop a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model of heat, force, material flow and defect formation.
Train two multilayer perceptron networks on experimental temperature and axial force histories.
Combine simulation and ANN predictions to map defective and defect-free welding conditions.
evidence_signal: Experimental validation showed good CEL agreement, ANN R² values of 0.91–0.99, and a peak plunge-force reduction from 1600 N to approximately 1100 N with 60 °C preheating.
watch_item: Prediction accuracy is demonstrated within the tested parameter space; extrapolation to other HDPE grades, joint geometries or operating conditions requires validation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
